intended_object: The integral vectors of a rational subspace U ⊆ V_ℚ: the ℤ-submodule {x ∈ V_ℤ | ι_ℚ(x) ∈ U} of the integral module, i.e. U ∩ V_ℤ (its preimage under the rationalization map). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation, which uses it as the integral carrier of sub-Hodge structures.
explanation: The body is `(U.restrictScalars ℤ).comap ιℚ`. This is exactly the preimage of U under the ℤ-linear rationalization map, and `mem_integralSubmodule` holds by `Iff.rfl`. It matches the standard construction, U ∩ V_ℤ, taken without any torsion-freeness hypothesis, so it is also right when ι_ℚ is not injective. The setting (an abelian group with a ℤ-linear map into a ℚ-vector space) is the natural one for the Hodge-structure application. Mathlib has no named counterpart: the definition is just a thin wrapper around Mathlib's general `Submodule.comap` and `restrictScalars`. So it is neither too narrow nor wrong.
